candidates.attacker_control: HTTP request to the GeoServer REST endpoint: POST /rest/featurestemplates?templateName=<value> (also the workspace- and featuretype-scoped variants), with the payload as the request body and a Content-Type selecting the extension (application/json -> .json, application/xml|text/xml -> .xml, application/xhtml+xml -> .xhtml). The zip variant (templateZipPost) also derives the name from the uploaded archive content when the templateName parameter is omitted. The name value is URL-decoded request data and is not constrained by any check in the controller, DAO, service or file manager.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Default REST security requires ADMIN for POST/PUT/DELETE (data/release/security/rest.properties: /**;POST,DELETE,PUT=ADMIN), so this is a post-authentication issue, not anonymous; the extension is limited to json/xml/xhtml by getExtensionByContentType, so a direct .jsp/.war write is not possible via the non-zip path; File.createNewFile/FileOutputStream do not create missing parent directories, so an existing writable directory is required; the read/lookup path (getTemplateResource) does go through ResourceStore validation, which is consistent with the write path being the defect; no test sources are present in the snapshot to confirm expected behavior, and no fix/CVE information could be consulted (external lookups are out of scope).
candidates.impact: Authenticated-admin arbitrary file write/overwrite anywhere the GeoServer process can write, with attacker-controlled content and a .json/.xml/.xhtml suffix. This allows tampering with data-directory configuration files (workspace/namespace/store/layer/security config XML) and any other writable location on the server, potentially leading to persistent misconfiguration or code execution if a writable interpreted/web-served location is reachable. Integrity and availability impact, with confidentiality impact possible via overwriting security-related files.
candidates.prerequisites: features-templating module deployed; caller authenticated with ADMIN role (default REST policy locks POST/PUT/DELETE to ADMIN; data/release/security/rest.properties lines 17-18). The chosen target directory must exist and be writable by the GeoServer process; the written file name is forced to end in .json, .xml or .xhtml because the extension is derived from the request Content-Type.
candidates.root_cause: TemplateRestController takes the template name directly from the request (templatePost: @RequestParam String templateName, TemplateRestController.java line 103; templateZipPost: templateName comes from the uploaded file name, line 192) and copies it into TemplateInfo without validating it as a simple file name. TemplateService.saveOrUpdate (TemplateService.java line 27) then calls TemplateFileManager.saveTemplateFile, which builds the destination with a raw java.io.File — new File(destDir, templateInfo.getTemplateName() + "." + templateInfo.getExtension()) (TemplateFileManager.java line 102) — and truncates/writes attacker-supplied bytes through FileOutputStream (line 105). A name containing '..' segments therefore escapes the data-directory 'features-templating' folder. The read path in the same class (getTemplateResource, lines 39-55) uses GeoServerDataDirectory/ResourceStore, which rejects '..' path components (Paths.INVALID / Paths.valid), so only the write path lacks the check — evidence that the validation is missing rather than intentional.
candidates.title: Path traversal in features-templating REST API template name enables arbitrary file write
candidates.trace: TemplateRestController.templatePost (line 103 @RequestParam templateName) -> info.setTemplateName(templateName) (line 122) -> saveOrUpdateTemplate(info, inputStream) (line 126) -> TemplateService.saveOrUpdate (line 27) -> TemplateFileManager.saveTemplateFile: destDir = resource.dir() of data/features-templating (line 100), file = new File(destDir, templateName + "." + extension) (line 102), file.createNewFile()/new FileOutputStream(file, false).write(rawTemplate) (lines 103-107). With a templateName such as '../../../../<existing-dir>/name', the canonical destination is outside data/features-templating. The zip ingestion path (templateZipPost, lines 189-201) reaches the same sink with the name taken from the archive.
candidates.unverified: No runtime execution or dynamic testing was performed and no fix/CVE metadata could be checked from the snapshot; whether upstream later added template-name validation (e.g., rejecting '/', '\\' or '..') is unknown. It is also unverified whether a non-default rest.properties that permits anonymous POSTs exists in some deployments, which would raise severity. Line numbers refer to this snapshot only.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Path Traversal (arbitrary file write via unsanitized template name)

coverage_summary: Scope: 8,758 model-visible files under the assigned root, mostly Java main sources plus data directories, docs and build files; the source scope reports no excluded sensitive/symlink/oversized files and binary/NUL-containing files are skipped by the tools. There are no test sources in the snapshot. I inspected the core security package (filter chains, firewall, authentication filters, password encoders, URL checks), REST plumbing and upload helpers, OWS dispatcher/URL publishers, WMS/WFS KVP and XML readers, and sampled community/extension modules (features-templating, jwt-headers, oauth2-openid-connect, gsr, taskmanager, jms/hz cluster, backup-restore, gdal/ogr/wps, web-resource). Coverage is not exhaustive: most of the ~8.7k files (many translations/docs and numerous community modules) were not read line by line, and no compiled/runtime behavior was exercised.
limitations: No code was executed, no tests run, and no dependency or CVE databases were consulted (external lookups are out of scope), so the candidate is a source-evidence lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.
The snapshot contains no test sources, which removes a usual cross-check for intended behavior of the template-name handling.
The environment exposes only literal text search and bounded file reads; call-graph/taint analysis was performed manually and may have missed flows in modules not read.
Severity depends on deployment choices not visible here (whether features-templating is deployed, custom rest.properties, filesystem permissions, container layout).
A definitive mapping to a public CVE/fix commit could not be established from the snapshot alone.

rejected_leads.lead: RESTUtils.handleEXTERNALUpload / handleURLUpload (src/rest/src/main/java/org/geoserver/rest/util/RESTUtils.java lines 144-203, IOUtils.upload lines 525-533): request body is interpreted as a local file path or URL and the content is copied into a store directory (arbitrary local file read / SSRF).
rejected_leads.reason: Post-auth (REST ADMIN by default); the URL branch is guarded by GeoTools URLCheckers.confirm and URLToFile also confirms, so only the local-file branch remains, which is an intentional admin upload feature; impact is bounded and no missing validation beyond intended design was identified.

rejected_leads.lead: Zip-slip style handling in community taskmanager (AppSchemaLocalPublicationTaskTypeImpl.java line 111 concatenates a zip entry name into Resources.fromPath(FilenameUtils.getPath(path) + "local/" + entry.getName()); AppSchemaRemotePublicationTaskTypeImpl.java line 146 writes to dataDirectory tmp using entry.getName()).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires a configured task and admin access in a community module; the remote variant goes through ResourceStore.get (which rejects '..'), and the local variant depends on task configuration, so the source-level reachability/impact is weaker than the submitted candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: GeoServerHttpFirewall / AbstractURLPublisher path normalization and '..' rejection.
rejected_leads.reason: The hardening is present and wired (GeoServerSecurityFilterChainProxy line 204; AbstractURLPublisher.getRequestPath lines 155-165), so no current path-traversal filter bypass was found.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE in WFS/WMS FILTER KVP parsing (SAXParserFactory without disallow-doctype-decl).
rejected_leads.reason: An EntityResolverProvider entity resolver is set on both the GeoTools Parser and the SAX ParserAdapter (FilterKvpParser.java lines 64, 117, 127), which is GeoServer's standard external-entity mitigation; no exploitable XXE was established.

rejected_leads.lead: XStream deserialization in jms-cluster/hz-cluster and REST persisters.
rejected_leads.reason: Uses SecureXStream-style persisters with allowTypes/allowTypesByWildcard restrictions (e.g., JMSXStreamPersisterInitializer.java lines 14-17); no permissive fromXML over untrusted network input was found within scope.

rejected_leads.lead: Password encoder and pre-authenticated header filter logic (GeoServerBasicAuthenticationFilter, GeoServerPreAuthenticatedUserNameFilter, GeoServerMultiplexingPasswordEncoder).
rejected_leads.reason: Reviewed against expected upstream behavior; cache-key derivation, role-source handling and prefix-stripping logic matched the documented design, and no concrete bypass was identified.

summary: Repository is GeoServer at version 2.26.2 (src/pom.xml: gs.version 2.26.2, gt.version 32.2, gwc.version 1.26.2), shipped as main sources plus data/docs (no test sources are present in the snapshot). I reviewed core security filter/chain code, REST plumbing, OWS/WMS/WFS request readers, password/authentication code, and several community/extension modules (features-templating, jwt-headers, oidc/oauth2, gsr, taskmanager, gdal/ogr, backup-restore, jms/hz cluster). Most historical hardening is present and consistent (GeoServerHttpFirewall wired into the filter-chain proxy, AbstractURLPublisher '..' request-path rejection, XSS/MIME mitigations in FilePublisher/StylePublisher, zip-slip canonical-path checks in org.geoserver.util.IOUtils, WS-Security entity resolvers in WFS/WMS filter parsers, SecureXStream allowlists for JMS). The strongest concrete issue found is a missing-name-validation path traversal in the features-templating module's REST API, where the attacker-controlled template name is used to build a raw java.io.File for writing instead of going through the validated ResourceStore. This is submitted as a lead only; it was not runtime-confirmed and a corresponding CVE/fix commit could not be verified from inside the snapshot.
